account: Today has been mostly routine mayoral business, with an unusual amount of discussion about grain deliveries and possible bridge or port changes. I have not established any actual change or transport need. The secretary reported that the builder found no confirmed hazard, work or costs; the baker denied announcing changes and confirmed normal operations. The innkeeper apparently had only an unspecified rumour. I also heard a fragment about a bridge or port change near the bakery, but not enough to establish what was meant. At the mill I saw two stacks of 64 hay bales in the stall chest. No grain transport was authorized. Neighbour and freight have discussed the matter, and neighbour has passed along my clarification that no crossing change is confirmed. This seems to be circulating news or rumour rather than a demonstrated project; I do not know its origin or purpose. Today's scheduled council letters have not materialized: the secretary reports no delivered correspondence and all four great hall table chests empty. I have no evidence explaining that absence. I attended tea with neighbour and returned for afternoon office business. The secretary needed a writable book to make a permanent record, so I bought and delivered one. I have just asked that today's confirmed findings and lack of transport or repair authorization be recorded and secured in the appointments chest, and asked whether any business remains before my nineteen o'clock return home.
